verdict.rationale: Homebrew documents real bulk operations. `brew bundle` installs every dependency in a Brewfile with one command, `brew bundle dump` snapshots all installed packages, `brew untap` removes one or more taps, and autoremove clears unneeded dependencies. Community reports confirm that `brew upgrade` updates all casks at once. Bulk coverage is mainly documented for install and snapshot workflows, so the full set of item operations is not shown. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of bulk upgrade and uninstall across selected item sets, and filtering or selection controls for bulk actions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: It allows you to tell users to run a single command to install all dependencies for a project and start any services.
`Brewfile`s can also be used as a way of saving all supported packages into a single file.
